question: What aircraft type operated flight 3851 PHX-SFO on 2026-01-03, and how many passengers had to be rebooked because of the delay?

input.sql: SELECT * FROM flights WHERE flight_date='2026-01-03' AND flight_number='3851' AND origin='PHX'
SELECT flight_id, tail_number, origin, destination, sched_dep_local, dep_delay_minutes, arr_delay_minutes, status FROM flights WHERE flight_number='3851' ORDER BY sched_dep_utc

SELECT r.flight_id, r.origin, r.destination, r.sched_dep_utc, f.dep_delay_minutes, f.arr_delay_minutes, f.delay_late_aircraft, f.delay_nas, f.status FROM rotation_sequence r JOIN flights f USING(flight_id) WHERE r.tail_number='N8633A' AND r.sched_dep_utc >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-01-03 15:00:00+00' ORDER BY r.sched_dep_utc LIMIT 12

content.text:
Neither of those two things is in this extract, so I can't answer them.

**Aircraft type: not available.** The BTS On-Time Performance extract carries the tail number but no fleet type or subtype. Flight 3851 PHX–SFO on 2026-01-03 (`2026-01-03|WN|3851|PHX|SFO|0855`) was operated by tail **N8633A**. Getting the type would need an outside registry lookup (FAA N-number registry or a fleet database) keyed on N8633A — nothing in this data supports it.

**Passengers rebooked: not available.** There is no passenger, booking, or misconnect data here at all — only schedule, times, delay minutes, and cause attribution. No amount of querying this extract will produce a rebooking count; that would have to come from the reservations/DCS system.

What I can give you on that flight is the operational picture. It pushed 142 minutes on departure (scheduled 08:55 PHX, off at 11:17 local) and landed 141 late at SFO, with all 141 minutes attributed to **NAS** — carrier, weather, late-aircraft and security were all zero, and the inbound leg that morning (`2026-01-03|WN|3851|MSY|PHX|0540`, same tail) arrived 11 minutes *early*, so this delay originated at PHX, not upstream.

It then cascaded down N8633A's whole remaining day, five more legs, all coded late_aircraft:

- `2026-01-03|WN|4106|SFO|PHX|1055` — dep 144, arr 134 (133 late_aircraft)
- `2026-01-03|WN|172|PHX|LGB|1440` — dep 135, arr 128 (128)
- `2026-01-03|WN|65|LGB|LAS|1545` — dep 140, arr 133 (124)
- `2026-01-03|WN|65|LAS|DAL|1735` — dep 144, arr 126 (116)
- `2026-01-03|WN|65|DAL|HOU|2255` — dep 155, arr 139 (114)

The tail reset overnight at HOU and departed the next morning on time (`2026-01-04|WN|2999|HOU|STL|0500`, +3). So the delay's operational footprint is six legs and roughly 800 minutes of accumulated arrival delay — but how many passengers that stranded is outside this data.
